Trace, implement and test: Find Roots

Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

Original source context
// C++ program to find roots of a quadratic equation
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

// Prints roots of quadratic equation ax*2 + bx + x
void findRoots(int a, int b, int c)
{
    // If a is 0, then equation is not quadratic, but
    // linear
    if (a == 0) {
        cout << "Invalid";
        return;
    }

    int d = b * b - 4 * a * c;
    double sqrt_val = sqrt(abs(d));

    if (d > 0) {
        cout << "Roots are real and different \n";
        cout << (double)(-b + sqrt_val) / (2 * a) << "\n"
             << (double)(-b - sqrt_val) / (2 * a);
    }
    else if (d == 0) {
        cout << "Roots are real and same \n";
        cout << -(double)b / (2 * a);
    }
    else // d < 0
    {
        cout << "Roots are complex \n";
        cout << -(double)b / (2 * a) << " + i"
             << sqrt_val / (2 * a) << "\n"
             << -(double)b / (2 * a) << " - i"
             << sqrt_val / (2 * a);
    }
}

// Driver code
int main()
{
    int a = 1, b = -7, c = 12;

    // Function call
    findRoots(a, b, c);
    return 0;
}
